portInfo.description: Port of Seattle operates two Alaska-season cruise terminals: Smith Cove at Pier 91 north of downtown and Bell Street at Pier 66 on the central waterfront. Pier 91’s place page lists 2001 W Garfield Way (and also shows 2001 West Garfield Street wording on the same page), describes a ground-transportation lot for buses/taxis/shuttles/private drop-off, complimentary shuttle from parking to terminal, and explicitly states public transit is not available to Pier 91. Pier 66 lists 2225 Alaskan Way, curb-lane drop-off on Alaskan Way with a security officer directing traffic, and general parking at $30 per day not including taxes via the cited parking operator. Passenger Information frames Seattle as an Alaska cruise home port with roughly 35 minutes from SEA to hotels/terminals in marketing copy. Door pins remain null.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Pike Place Market — walkable framing from Pier 66; transfer from Pier 91 — ~120 min.
Seattle waterfront / Great Wheel area — Pier 66 adjacent context.
Chihuly / Space Needle — Seattle Center; transfer minutes Not verified.
Museum of Pop Culture / Chihuly cluster — mid call.
Ferry to Bainbridge — only with long buffer and schedule discipline.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Pier 91 is not a downtown walk-off. If your documents say Smith Cove / Pier 91, budget a transfer before you plan Pike Place as “steps away”.
